chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Ismail ibn Jabir or Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I stand [for prayer] at the end of the night, and I fear the morning [will come before I finish].' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Recite Al-Hamd [Surah Al-Fatiha], and hasten, and hasten.'

key_terms.آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ: the end of the night (time for Tahajjud)
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatiha, the essential recitation in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they fear dawn will come before finishing night prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the practical dilemma of Tahajjud worshippers who risk missing the Fajr prayer due to lengthy recitations. By instructing them to read only Al-Fatiha and 'hasten' (wa'ajil), the Imam emphasizes the principle of *fada'il al-a'mal* (superiority of action) and the importance of preserving the obligatory prayer's time over voluntary prolongation. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with the timely fulfillment of religious duties.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Al-Hajjal, from Abdullah Bin Al-Waleed Al-Kindy, from Ismail Bin Jabir, or Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I stand (for Salāt) at the end of the night, and I fear the morning’. Heasws said: ‘Recite Al-Hamd (Chapter 1), and hasten, and hasten’.
en.sarwar: 27. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al- Kindiy from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir or ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I get up in the end of the night and I fear (of the coming of dawn before completing).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Recite just al-Fatihah, and make it faster and faster.’”
